text: Feed the Kraken is a social deduction game for 5 to 11 players. In Feed the Kraken each player secretly receives the role of either Sailor, Pirate or Cult Leader and uses all available means to plot the course of the ship towards their faction's destination. Every turn the ship will sail in one of the three possible directions. Players will take turns as captain, lieutenant or navigator, each having the chance to manipulate the course of the ship. Players will use and witness cabin searches, mutinies, the silencing of adversaries and even sacrifices to the ancient Kraken God. All players use their deduction skills to find out whom to trust.

Game contents: 1 double-sided game board (Quick Journey and Long Journey), 1 ship, 1 captain's logbook, 40 guns, 22 character cards, 23 navigation cards, 4 crew overview cards, 4 flogging cards (the 'I am not a...' card, Pirate card, Sailor card, Cult card), 5 cult ritual cards (3 Conversion to Cult, 1 The Cult's Guns Stash, 1 Cult Cabin Search), 7 map action tokens (4 Cabin Search, 2 Flogging, 1 Off with the Tongue), 3 off-duty signs. The 23 navigation cards are: 4 Blue Drunk, 2 Blue Disarmed, 6 Yellow Cult Uprising, 5 Red Drunk, 2 Red Mermaid, 2 Red Telescope, 2 Red Armed. Faction chips: 5 Sailor (blue), 4 Pirate (red), 1 Cult Leader (yellow), 1 Cultist (green). Each player also has a seabag to hold their faction chip secretly.

Use the quick journey map for 5, 6 and 7 player games. Regardless of player count, you should play your first game on the quick journey map to get a feeling for the game. Once familiar, you may switch to the long journey map for games with 7 or more players. Preparing the map: Place the ship on the starting area in the south. Place the map action tokens on the corresponding areas on the map: 3 Cabin Search and 2 Feed the Kraken. Shuffle the 5 cult ritual cards and place them face down spread out on the edge of the game board. Depending on the number of players, set aside the appropriate number of off-duty signs: 5-6 players use 1 off-duty sign, 7-8 players use 2, 9-11 players use 3. Remove 1 Cult Uprising (yellow), 1 Drunk (blue) and 2 Armed (red) from the navigation deck; these 4 cards are not used on the quick journey map. Shuffle only the remaining 19 navigation cards as the draw pile on the map archive: North (yellow) 5 Cult Uprising; East (blue) 3 Drunk and 2 Disarmed; West (red) 5 Drunk, 2 Mermaid and 2 Telescope. Each player receives 3 guns.

section: Setup - Secret Teams and 5 Player Rules
text: Distribution of the secret teams: Depending on the number of players, place the corresponding The Crew card next to the map. Find the right number of Sailor, Pirate and Cult Leader chips and put each one in a separate bag. Shuffle the bags and distribute one to each player. Each player secretly checks their seabag; their chip determines their team membership. 5 Player Rules: When playing with 5 players, the team composition can vary. There are either 3 Sailors, 1 Pirate and 1 Cult Leader, or 2 Sailors, 2 Pirates and 1 Cult Leader. To realize this, prepare bags with 3 Sailor and 2 Pirate faction chips and shuffle them carefully. Remove a random bag without revealing its content, then add the bag with the Cult Leader chip and shuffle again. Each player receives one bag. During the secret pirate gathering the Pirates learn how many they actually are; all other players try to find out the actual team constellation during the game.

Use the long journey map for games with 7 or more players. Place the ship on the starting area in the south. Place the map action tokens on the corresponding areas on the map: 4 Cabin Search, 2 Flogging, 1 Off with the Tongue and 3 Feed the Kraken. Shuffle the 5 cult ritual cards and place them face down spread out on the edge of the game board. Set aside off-duty signs by player count: 7-8 players use 2 off-duty signs, 9-11 players use 3. To prepare for navigation, shuffle all 23 navigation cards as the draw pile: North (yellow) 6 Cult Uprising; East (blue) 4 Drunk and 2 Disarmed; West (red) 5 Drunk, 2 Mermaid, 2 Telescope and 2 Armed. Each player receives 3 guns. Place the 'I am not a...' card and the 3 small flogging cards next to the map.

Team compositions overview by player count. 5 players: 3 or 2 Sailors, 1 or 2 Pirates, 1 Cult Leader, no Cultist. 6 players: 3 Sailors, 2 Pirates, 1 Cult Leader. 7 players: 4 Sailors, 2 Pirates, 1 Cult Leader. 8 players: 4 Sailors, 3 Pirates, 1 Cult Leader. 9 players: 5 Sailors, 3 Pirates, 1 Cult Leader. 10 players: 5 Sailors, 4 Pirates, 1 Cult Leader. 11 players: 5 Sailors, 4 Pirates, 1 Cult Leader and 1 Cultist. After receiving teams, players receive their character cards: set aside the Captain card, shuffle the other character cards and set aside one card less than the number of players, add the Captain card and shuffle. Deal one card face down to each player. The player with the Captain card reveals it immediately, becomes the first captain, and receives a random new character card. The captain takes the captain's logbook, the lieutenant badge and the navigator badge.

The following victory conditions apply to the teams. Sailors: All Sailors win as a team if the ship reaches Bluewater Bay, the blue area in the east. Pirates: All Pirates win as a team if the ship reaches Crimson Cove, the red area in the west. Cult Leader and Cultists: The Cult wins as a team if the ship reaches the enormous Kraken in the north (Cult Victory), or when the Cult Leader is sacrificed to the Kraken on one of the Feed the Kraken spaces. Players always win together with their team, even if they went overboard before the end of the game.

section: The Secret Gathering of the Pirates
text: The Secret Gathering of the Pirates: Before the game begins, the Pirates secretly and silently find out who their Pirate teammates are. One player reads the following with everyone's eyes closed: 'All players close their eyes.' 'Pirates, open your eyes and memorize your team members.' The Pirates have about 20 seconds to find each other. 'Pirates, close your eyes.' 'All players now open their eyes.' There is no secret gathering of the cult. In a game with 11 players, the Cult Leader and the first Cultist do not know each other's identity at the start of the game; they have to find each other during the game, just like the Sailors.

Gameplay phases each round: 1. Appointing the navigation team, 2. A question of loyalty, 3. The navigation, 4. Off-duty. Appointing the Navigation Team: The captain cannot navigate the ship alone and needs two crew members. The captain chooses a player and hands them the lieutenant badge, then chooses a second player and hands them the navigator badge. Exceptions: the captain can not appoint himself; off-duty players can not be appointed; lieutenant and navigator can not be the same person.

A Question of Loyalty: The crew does not have to accept the captain's choices. If the crew doesn't trust the captain's chosen team, they can mutiny against them with their guns. The captain asks the crew about their loyalty. The required sum of guns for a successful mutiny depends on player count: with 5 to 7 players, 3 or more guns; with 8 to 9 players, 4 or more guns; with 10 to 11 players, 5 or more guns. The number of guns each player has is secret information during the mutiny, but outside of a mutiny it is public and all players must keep their guns visibly on the table. Steps: Each crew member except the captain secretly places 0 or more guns in one fist. All hold their closed fist over the table. The captain counts to 3, all open their fists and reveal their guns. The captain counts the total revealed guns and checks whether the mutiny is successful.

Resolving a Mutiny: If a mutiny is successful, whoever revealed the most guns wins the mutiny and becomes the new captain. In the case of a tie, all players tied for the most guns raise their hands; the captain still in office selects one tied winner who lowers their hand and won't become captain, repeating until only one winner remains, who becomes the new captain. All players involved in a successful mutiny must discard all of their revealed guns, including the player who just became captain. The current round ends and the new captain starts a new round by appointing the navigation team. The new captain can also be mutinied against after announcing the navigation team. You can become captain while off-duty; if the new captain is off-duty, the off-duty sign has no effect while they remain captain. If there is no mutiny (the total revealed guns were not enough), all players return their guns to their personal supply and the captain carries out The Navigation.

The Navigation: The captain, lieutenant and navigator navigate the ship together. The captain draws the top two navigation cards face down from the draw pile. The lieutenant then draws the next two cards face down. Both players look at their cards and choose one to discard face down into the deep sea (the discard pile). They each place their other card face down next to each other in the captain's logbook. The logbook is closed and shaken to shuffle the two cards, then passed to the navigator. The navigator secretly looks at the two cards in the logbook and discards one into the deep sea face down. The navigator leaves their preferred card in the logbook and returns it to the captain. The captain reveals the remaining card to the crew and takes the resulting actions. During navigation the selected players must remain silent and may not give any signs or signals. Only after the captain reveals the last navigation card may players talk about the cards they allegedly drew and discarded.

Executing the Navigation Card: The captain places the chosen card in front of them as part of the captain's official resume; it remains openly visible until the end of the game and is never shuffled back into the navigation pile. The captain executes the effects in this order: I. Move the ship in the direction of the colored arrow on the current map space that corresponds to the color of the navigation card (blue moves east, red moves west, yellow moves north). II. If there is an icon on the space the ship moved to, take that map action next. III. Take the action corresponding to the icon on the navigation card.

Off-duty: After navigation, certain players take a break and receive an off-duty sign depending on the number of players at the start of the game. 5-6 players: 1 off-duty sign, given to the navigator. 7-8 players: 2 off-duty signs, given to the lieutenant and the navigator. 9-11 players: 3 off-duty signs, given to the captain, lieutenant and navigator. Give the off-duty signs to the players involved in the current navigation. Players who were previously off-duty become available again for the next navigation. Rules: As long as an off-duty sign is in front of a player, they cannot be chosen as navigator or lieutenant. Off-duty signs are only passed on after a successful navigation, not after a mutiny. Off-duty players can participate in a mutiny and can become captain. If the captain has an off-duty sign, it is not relevant as long as that player remains captain. Off-duty signs are ignored if there aren't enough available players left for the captain to choose a navigation team.

section: The Next Game Round and Reshuffle
text: The Next Game Round Begins: The navigator and lieutenant badges are handed back to the current captain, who starts the next round by appointing the navigation team. All phases are carried out again each round. Reshuffle: If there are fewer than 4 cards in the draw pile before navigation, combine the remaining draw pile with the discard pile, keep all cards face down, and shuffle them thoroughly into a new draw pile. The remaining cards may not be inspected when combined and shuffled. The face-up cards in front of the players (the captain's resume) are never shuffled back into the draw pile. The character cards Archivist, Smuggler and Look-Out can cause you to run out of cards during a navigation despite having at least 4 cards before; in that rare case you reshuffle once the draw pile is empty.

Denial of Command: If the navigator doesn't want to execute the commands of the captain and lieutenant, he can refuse by jumping overboard. Denial of command is allowed throughout the entire game and takes place during The Navigation after the navigator has seen both navigation cards. The navigator states that they will not carry out the commands but jump overboard instead. They place both navigation cards face down in the discard pile instead of passing one back to the captain. The navigator is immediately eliminated from the game and must remain silent until the end of the game; they may not reveal their faction nor any knowledge about the discarded navigation cards. Then an Emergency Navigation must be carried out. The Cult Leader can not win by jumping overboard as the navigator, even if this happens on a Feed the Kraken space.

The Emergency Navigation: After a denial of command, the captain must immediately designate an emergency navigator. Due to this exceptional situation, the captain can even choose an off-duty player. The crew can not mutiny against the chosen emergency navigator; there is no Question of Loyalty. The lieutenant stays the same for the emergency navigation. The captain, lieutenant and emergency navigator immediately carry out another navigation. If the emergency navigator jumps ship as well, the captain keeps choosing emergency navigators until a navigation is successfully completed. After a successful emergency navigation, the game continues as normal starting with Appointing the Navigation Team. If the number of remaining players on the ship ever falls below three, any open position is resolved randomly by the captain.

Supply Line: The supply line only exists on the long journey map. As soon as the ship crosses the supply line, each player can refill their gun supply up to three guns by taking the required number of guns from the general supply. If a player still has three or more guns at this point, they will not receive any additional guns.

The End of the Game: The navigation rounds are repeated until one of the victory conditions is met. Players reveal their faction at the end of the game by showing each other the faction chips from their seabags. Players always win together with their team, even if they went overboard before the end of the game.

Map Actions: Every time the ship reaches a new space, check whether it shows an icon. The corresponding action is carried out during navigation, immediately after the captain has moved the ship but before performing the navigation card action. The captain may discuss options with the crew but always makes the final decision. Cabin Search: The captain chooses another player and hands them the cabin search token. The selected player must pass their seabag to the captain for a secret inspection while everybody else closes their eyes. The captain may talk about their findings, but might be lying. Important: A player affected by the Cabin Search can not be turned into a Cultist anymore. A player who has already become a Cultist before the cabin search signals this to the captain with a tentacle gesture.

section: Map Actions - Off with the Tongue
text: Off with the Tongue: The captain chooses another player and hands them the off with the tongue token. That player is no longer allowed to articulate words, but can make sounds and gesticulate. They can also no longer become captain. The following rules apply: When a new captain is determined via the Drunk action on a navigation card, the player without tongue is ignored. The player continues to participate in mutinies; their guns count normally for the total mutiny score, but while determining the next captain their gun count is always treated as 0 guns.

Flogging: The Flogging creates public information for all players. It indicates one of the factions the selected player does not belong to. Steps: The captain chooses another player to undergo the Flogging and hands them the three small flogging cards. The player shuffles the cards face down, then looks at them and chooses the card with the colored icon that corresponds to their current faction and places it face down: red as a Pirate, blue as a Sailor, yellow or green as a Cult Leader or Cultist. The flogged player shuffles the other two cards and places them face down. The captain randomly picks one of the two cards and reveals it. The card indicates a faction the selected player does not belong to; place it on top of the 'I am not a...' card in front of the flogged player. This information is public and remains until the end of the game. Important: A player affected by the Flogging can not be turned into a Cultist anymore.

Feed the Kraken: When the captain has made up their mind, the captain chooses another player and places the Feed the Kraken token in front of them. That player is immediately eliminated from the game and must not speak anymore or reveal their faction. Important: The captain must not choose themself. If the Cult Leader is selected to be fed to the Kraken, the Cult Leader and all of their Cultists immediately win the game.

section: Navigation Card Actions - Drunk and Mermaid
text: Navigation Card Actions are carried out during the navigation phase, immediately after the map action. Drunk: The current captain loses their position. The captain role moves clockwise to the next player who has the fewest navigation cards (resumes) in front of them. Pass the captain's logbook to the new captain. Mermaid: The captain chooses another player. That player shuffles the last three discarded navigation cards and secretly looks at them. They may and should talk about their findings, but they might be lying.

section: Navigation Card Actions - Telescope, Armed, Disarmed, Cult Uprising
text: Telescope: The captain chooses another player. That player looks at the top navigation card of the draw pile. They may put the card back on the draw pile or discard it into the Deep Sea. Armed: The navigator receives 1 gun from the general supply. These Armed cards are only used on the long journey map. Disarmed: The navigator must discard 1 gun from their personal supply if they have any. Cult Uprising: A cult ritual is carried out at the end of the navigation. To do this, the captain must reveal a cult ritual card.

Cult Ritual Cards: Every time a navigation card with Cult Uprising has been played in the navigation, the captain must reveal a random face-down cult ritual card at the end of the navigation. The Cult's Guns Stash: The Cult Leader secretly distributes three guns from the supply to any number of up to three players. Place three guns from the supply in the center of the table, all players close their eyes and extend a flat hand over the center, the Cult Leader opens their eyes and puts the guns in the hands of up to three players. They can choose any player including themselves and may give more than one gun to a player. Cult Cabin Search: The Cult Leader secretly learns about the factions of the current navigation team. All players close their eyes and the Cult Leader opens their eyes; keeping their eyes closed, the current captain, lieutenant and navigator all reveal their faction chip. The Cult Leader gets 30 seconds to see the three players' factions, then the team hides their chips again. Conversion to Cult: The Cult Leader converts another player to their Cult. From now on the chosen player is a Cultist instead of a Sailor or Pirate, and wins or loses together with the Cult Leader.

Becoming a Cultist: When the cult ritual card Conversion to Cult is revealed, the Cult Leader secretly adds another player to their team by turning them into a Cultist. The captain recites text instructing every convertible player to put a fist over the center of the table, all players close their eyes including the captain, the Cult Leader opens their eyes and chooses a convertible player, touches their chosen player's fist with their tentacle fingers, and the selected player becomes a Cultist. Rules: The Cult Leader can only convert convertible players. Every player who has previously been examined in a Cabin Search or Flogging counts as unconvertible. The new Cultist loses their previous team membership and is no longer a Pirate or Sailor; they can only win together with the Cult Leader by fulfilling one of the cult victory conditions. Any additional Cultists do not open their eyes during this process, only the Cult Leader and the new Cultist.

Character Cards: Each player receives a character card at the start of the game. These remain facedown in front of the players until they are used. Players can reveal their character card strategically at any point in the game to receive a unique effect, though timing restrictions may apply. To activate, flip and reveal the card; only unflipped (facedown) character cards may be activated. After activation the card remains revealed. A character can only be activated once, unless it gets turned facedown by an effect. Most character cards can only be used once but at any time; some have timing restrictions and a few have recurring or ongoing effects. Some characters work better with certain player numbers; for example, avoid using Debt Collector, Minstrel and Mentor in games with 5-6 players.

Strategy Advice: If you are a Pirate, argue and behave like a Sailor; you can bluff being a Sailor by selecting blue cards while navigating, but don't be afraid to sail westwards at crucial moments. Unlike other social deduction games, staying under the radar doesn't achieve enough; Pirates need to actively collaborate with the Cult and influence the course westwards. If you are the Cult Leader, balance the direction of travel towards the center of the map so you reach the Feed the Kraken spaces or your victory space, switching between helping the Pirates and the Sailors; yellow navigation cards grant opportunities to convert players. If you are a Sailor, stick to the truth and try to find out who else is on your side; there is no reason to pretend to be a Pirate.
